name: Thaur
kurzbeschreibung: Historic village featuring Burg Thaur, the Pestkreuzweg, and the expansive Naturpark below the Karwendel mountains.
beschreibung:
Overview

Thaur is situated at an elevation of 633 meters in the Tyrolean Inn Valley on the sunny southern slopes of the Nordkette range, right at the threshold of the Karwendel Nature Park. With around 4,100 inhabitants, the traditional village lies roughly eight kilometers east of Innsbruck and forms part of the historic MARTHA villages alongside Mühlau, Arzl, Rum, and Absam. Thaur is celebrated as Tyrol's primary vegetable garden: on the fertile valley soils, more than half of the province's field-grown vegetables thrive, including fresh salads, leeks, cabbage, and famous Thaur horseradish. The municipal territory stretches from the valley plains up to the Thaurer Zunterkopf at 1,918 meters, effortlessly harmonizing pastoral charm with alpine recreation.

History

Settlement in the area dates back to the Bronze Age and Roman times. The village was first documented in 827 AD as 'ad Taurane' in the will of nobleman Quartinus, making Thaur one of the oldest recorded communities in the Inn Valley. In the 12th century, the Counts of Andechs erected Castle Thaur atop a rocky spur overlooking the valley, serving as a regional court and safeguarding valuable salt transports from nearby Hall in Tirol. On the castle hill stands the Romedikirchl chapel, consecrated in 1636 and dedicated to Saint Romedius of Thaur. A plague pilgrimage path with 14 detailed wayside shrines leads uphill to the chapel, erected following a solemn vow during the 1636 epidemic. In the village center, the Parish Church of the Assumption showcases splendid Rococo frescoes designed under master builder Franz de Paula Penz. Thaur is also renowned for centuries-old nativity scene carving and the Thaurer Mullerlaufen carnival pageant, recognized as intangible UNESCO Cultural Heritage.

Getting There

By car, Thaur is easily reached via the Inntal Autobahn A12 by exiting at Hall-Mitte or Hall-West and following the B171 and local road L321. Drivers from Innsbruck arrive in less than ten minutes. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof or the regional railway station in Hall in Tirol. Regular VVT bus services 501, 502, and 503 operate every ten minutes connecting Innsbruck, Rum, Thaur, and Hall in Tirol.

Tips

A rewarding circular hike leads along the historic plague trail up to the Romedikirchl and the stone ruins of Castle Thaur, where open-air theater performances take place and the Romediwirt inn serves authentic Tyrolean specialties. More ambitious hikers can ascend further to the Thaurer Alm at 1,464 meters or tackle the trail toward the Kaisersäule monument, enjoying panoramic vistas of the Inn Valley. Stop by local farm shops to sample freshly harvested regional vegetables and genuine Thaur horseradish.
